text:
maria: Heads-up — canary for the Dedicated rollout is flapping p95 on heavyseq workloads, ops have put the rollout on hold :warning:
ajay: saw alerts too, p95 jumped from ~80ms to ~260ms after canary deploy around 15:02 UTC
linh: metrics snapshot from the canary nodes:
```\nCPU util: 78% -> 85%\nGPU SM util: stable
Host latency p95: 260ms (was 78ms)
KV cache hitrate: 91% -> 64%\nbatch size distribution shifted: more small-batches (~1-2)
```
tim: interesting that GPU SM stayed steady — points to either scheduling/batching or some host-side stall
maria: yeah, kernel-selection logs show a lot of fallbacks to slow-path kernels on long sequences after the recent selector change (adaptive-kernel-selector v1.4)
ajay: i ran a quick bisect locally. causality points to merge 2891 which changes the microbatch-slicer + kernel-hint policy. reverting that change locally restores p95 to ~82ms
linh: stack trace snippet from the canary profiler:
```
kernel_choice.cpp:234 choose_kernel_for_op() -> preferred: fast_path_conv, selected: fallback_conv_slow
batcher.cpp:87 slice_microbatch() -> slices increased x3 for many requests
kv_prefetcher.cpp:112 schedule_prefetch() -> prefetch miss spikes when slices < 4
```
maria: so the new slicer creates smaller microbatches which breaks prefetching and forces more kernel fallbacks -> more host scheduling overhead and p95 climb
perf-ci-bot: CI perf test "dedicated-p95-heavyseq" failed on merge 2891: p95 +210% (regression test run id: r-2026-47)
ajay: we should either revert 2891 or patch the selector to preserve the old slice thresholds for dedicated pools
tim: rollback plan: revert PR 2891 in canary, redeploy canary, wait 20 minutes for metrics, then slow rollout. who can open revert?
linh: I'll open revert PR now, but we should also add a guard: microbatch-slicer:force_min_slice=4 on dedicated pools until we have a robust heuristic
maria: agree. add a runtime knob so we don't need code revert if we want to toggle quickly
ajay: also suggest adding a short-term hotfix to kernel-selector: prefer fast_path when seq_len > 1024 or when batcher reports high small-batch ratio
perf-ci-bot: adding checklist item: add a unit/perf regression for microbatch distribution for next CI run
deploy-bot: canary rollout paused by ops (reason: p95 regression). ticket: #INC-6122
maria: action items: 1) lind to open revert PR 2891 (linh) 2) add runtime flag on dedicated pools (ajay) 3) backfill a CI perf test for microbatch distribution (tim) 4) notify affected customers (marcus from sales flagged 2 accounts)
linh: revert PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/merge_requests/2904 — will try to fast-track review
ajay: I'll draft the runtime-flag patch and put it behind a config: dedicated_force_min_slice=4
maria: if revert lands, we plan to redeploy canary in ~30m. oncall, please watch #metrics and notify if p95 doesn't recover in 15m after deploy
tim: I'll coordinate canary redeploy, will try to watch both canary dashboards and customer-facing latencies
linh: small note: this regression only shows up under dedicated pools with the new batching telemetry enabled — hosted path unaffected for now
ajay: filing a short postmortem template entry now: root cause = microbatch-slicer heuristics + kernel-selector fallback interplay; mitigations = revert, runtime guard, CI coverage, follow-up patch
maria: thanks. quick comms to support and sales: we should proactively notify the two flagged customers and let them know we have rollback in progress and an ETA of ~1h for stable canary redeploy
perf-ci-bot: scheduled extra perf run after revert merged to validate p95 recovery
maria: OK team — stay in this thread for updates. once canary is green we'll coordinate the dedicated rollout resume :white_check_mark:
